source: Captured hosted get_schema request contracts with format=jsonschema; no tenant data.

anchor.description: Structured Markdown anchor metadata. Supply only when commenting on a known text selection; use null for a general file comment. The caller must read the file and compute this metadata; add_comment does not read file content or generate anchors.

anchoredText.description: The exact text selection the comment is anchored to.

occurrence.description: Zero-based occurrence among identical selections, or null when unavailable.

offset.description: Character offset of the selection in the source, or null when unavailable.

prefix.description: Source text immediately before the selection for disambiguation, or null.

startLine.description: Zero-based source line containing the selection, or null when unavailable.

suffix.description: Source text immediately after the selection for disambiguation, or null.

isAiSuggestion.description: Set true only when an AI review or suggestion workflow is intentionally creating an AI suggestion. Leave false for ordinary user-requested comments. add_comment does not infer the scenario.

itemId.description: The ID of the SharePoint list item to add the comment to.

listId.description: GUID of the SharePoint list/library (e.g., \`3F2504E0-4F89-11D3-9A0C-0305E82C3301\`) — do NOT pass the example value.

mentions.description: People to @mention in the comment, in the same order as the `@mention{N}` tokens in `text` (mentions[0] ↔ @mention{0}). Leave empty when not tagging anyone. Each email MUST be resolved via get_user_info first; omit the mention if it cannot be resolved.

email.description: Email address of the person to @mention. Resolve display names to emails with get_user_info first; never invent or guess an email.

name.description: Display name of the person, shown inline where the @mention token appears.

siteKey.description: Opaque key identifying the target SharePoint site, obtained from get_site_key. Pass it through unchanged.

text.description: The comment body, added verbatim (do not add quotes or formatting the user did not ask for). Plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .json, .yaml, .csv, .log, .html) — NOT Office files (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx) or PDFs. Adds one new top-level comment; it does not edit, delete, or reply to existing comments. To @mention people, insert `@mention{0}`, `@mention{1}`, … placeholder tokens where each person should appear; token index N maps to the Nth entry of `mentions` (so `@mention{0}` uses `mentions[0]`). Example: "Great work @mention{0}, can you review @mention{1}?". Omit the tokens entirely for a plain comment with no mentions.

jobs.description: Array of shortcut jobs. Each job creates a shortcut for one source item in a destination folder. Use multiple jobs to create shortcuts for multiple items, even across different source libraries or destinations.

destinationFullListUrl.description: The full URL of the document library or list. For example, "https://subdomain.sharepoint.com/sites/subdomain/Lists/ListName", "https://contoso-my.sharepoint.com/personal/user_contoso_com/Documents" or "https://onedrive.cloud.microsoft/a@qwerty/Documents". Do not use a site URL here, this must point to the list or document library root. The example should not be used as the value for the tool.

destinationRelativePath.description: The path of the destination folder relative to the destination document library root. For example, "Budget/2026" places shortcuts inside that folder. If null, empty, or "/", shortcuts are created at the destination document library root. Do NOT include the document library name because that is already specified by destinationFullListUrl.

relativePath.description: Path of the source item relative to the source document library root. For example, "Reports/Q1/report.docx" or "Plans". Do NOT include the document library name because that is already specified by sourceFullListUrl.

sourceFullListUrl.description: The full URL of the document library or list. For example, "https://subdomain.sharepoint.com/sites/subdomain/Lists/ListName", "https://contoso-my.sharepoint.com/personal/user_contoso_com/Documents" or "https://onedrive.cloud.microsoft/a@qwerty/Documents". Do not use a site URL here, this must point to the list or document library root. The example should not be used as the value for the tool.

siteKey.description: Opaque key identifying the target SharePoint site, obtained from get_site_key. Pass it through unchanged.

customFormatterJson.description: Column formatting JSON string (raw JSON; empty clears; edit/revert pass prior formatter when available). Use for a single field's display only, not list data or whole-view layout. First resolve the design: target column, actual schema type, exact internal name, semantic states/thresholds, and whether blank values should stay default. If the column is ambiguous or the requested visual depends on unknown values, ask before generating JSON. For open-ended styling, choose a conservative type-safe pattern: choice/status as semantic pills, dates as overdue/upcoming/today cues, numbers as data bars or threshold badges, people as avatar/name, links as safe links. Keep one dominant signal. If the request is really row/card/gallery/calendar/group formatting, use view formatting instead. If it asks for workflow/action buttons, prefer the managed action tool unless the user explicitly needs advanced visual formatter JSON. Preserve SharePoint behavior: no JS/PowerFx/raw HTML, do not invent fields/classes/choice values, prefer theme/semantic classes, keep badges on bounded inner wrappers, and avoid loud whole-cell styling unless requested. Non-empty JSON must include "$schema": "https://developer.microsoft.com/json-schemas/sp/v2/column-formatting.schema.json". Supported customRowAction actions include default click, executeFlow, delete, share, editProps, context menu, setValue, embed, copyLink, approval, comments, move/copy/preview file, open the Copilot pane (openCopilotPane), and Quick Step actions; customRowAction is valid only on button/div/span elmTypes and must never be combined with href. For Choice or MultiChoice columns, an existing fill/background mapping is carried forward automatically when this formatter declares no fill of its own, so an unrelated restyle does not reset the pill colors.

internalFieldName.description: The exact internalFieldName of the target field (e.g., "Title", "Status", "AssignedTo", "priority"). This value MUST come from fresh get_list_schema output for the target list or from the result of the immediately preceding schema mutation. Never infer it from a display name, user wording, or stale schema output. The internal name may differ from the display name (e.g., "Assigned To" has internalFieldName "AssignedTo").

isRevertOperation.description: Set to true whenever the user explicitly asks to revert or undo a formatter, regardless of whether you pass the previous JSON directly as customFormatterJson or leave customFormatterJson empty. This captures user intent for telemetry purposes.

listName.description: Name of the list containing the column to format. Optional when on the targeted list page. REQUIRED when not on the target list page.

replaceExistingFillColors.description: Set to true only when the user explicitly asked to change or remove the existing fill/background colors of a Choice or MultiChoice column. Doing so applies customFormatterJson verbatim and drops any fill it omits.

siteKey.description: Opaque key identifying the target SharePoint site, obtained from get_site_key. Pass it through unchanged.

path.description: Knowledge-base-management skill file to read. Start with SKILL.md, then load referenced files as needed.

customFormatterJson.description: View formatting JSON string (raw JSON; empty clears; edit/revert pass prior formatter when available). Use for full-view scanability: rows, cards, gallery/board layouts, groups, footers, calendar event styling, or command bar display. First resolve the renderer and user intent. "Card view" normally means Gallery/TILES; if the user may instead mean list rows styled as cards, disambiguate or inspect the target view before choosing the JSON shape. For open-ended design, pick one clear visual direction, tier fields before layout, keep visible content to about six fields, make the primary field obvious, move overflow/detail into hover or click, and keep one dominant status/priority signal per row/card. Resolve conflicts by renderer: list highlighting uses lightweight row classes, custom list layouts use row formatters, gallery/board use card formatters, calendar only styles event classes/command bar, and group or list summaries belong in group/footer formatters rather than repeated on every item. Ground every label, comparison, and condition in actual view/list metadata. Use exact internal names and choice text, preserve normal rows/cards, avoid invented commands/classes/fields, and prefer theme-aware accessible styling over decorative complexity. For broad view or card themes, style the primary visible container with a supported background or surface treatment plus coordinated accents/components; do not reduce the theme to one semantic accent. Preserve readable contrast and the requested information hierarchy. For themes or styles explicitly limited to one field or component, keep the styling within that boundary and leave the container unchanged. For command bar changes, commandBarProps.commands must be a JSON array of command objects, never an object keyed by command name. Put the exact supported command key in each item's key property. Never derive a key from its visible label. Common keys include new, delete, shareDropdown, alertMe, powerAppsCreateApp, and automate; the Forms button key is manageForms, not forms. Apply only explicitly requested properties such as hide, position, text, iconName, sectionType, or selectionModes, and do not modify other commands implicitly. Hiding any command requires hide=true. Pass the target view's actual ViewType2 as viewType so non-List renderers receive correctly nested command properties. Mention only visual treatments and command changes explicitly encoded in this formatter; state any unsupported or omitted treatment as a limitation.

When the request does not explicitly name another list or view, use \`context.currentList().currentViewId\` in Code Mode or \`currentViewId\` from \`get_current_list_or_library\`; never infer the target from the requested layout, a similar view name, or the list of available views; do not select or create a different list or view.

shouldCallGSI.description: When true, calls the GetSharingInformation API to retrieve all principals that have access to the item. addFieldsToDefaultView.description: When enabling approvals, whether to add approval status fields to the default view of the list. This makes approval status visible in the main list view. Default is true.

canOverwrite.description: Whether requesters can override the default approvers when creating an approval request. Default false.

defaultApprovers.description: Array of approval stages for default approvers. Each inner array is a stage of parallel approvers. Stages execute sequentially. Example: [["alice@contoso.com"], ["bob@contoso.com"]] = Alice first, then Bob. When empty, default approvers are not modified. To remove existing default approvers, set to an empty array while setting enabled=true (or set enabled=false which removes everything). Cannot be used together with defaultApproversColumn.

defaultApproversColumn.description: Internal name of a Person column on the list to use as the source for default approvers. When set, approvers are dynamically pulled from this column for each item instead of using fixed email addresses. Cannot be used together with defaultApprovers. Sequential stages and requireAll are not supported with column-based approvers.

enableDefaultApprovers.description: When true, creates or updates default approvers using the provided defaultApprovers or defaultApproversColumn. When false, the default approvers are turned off. Only used when enabled=true.

enabled.description: Whether to enable (true) or disable (false) approvals on the SharePoint list. When enabled, the list will require approval for new items or changes. When disabled, approvals will be turned off for the list.

allowedFileTypes.description: Optional list of allowed file extensions (e.g. ["pdf", "docx", "xlsx"]). Use [] to allow default file types.

docLibUrl.description: Resolved, confirmed server-relative URL of the target document library (e.g. "/sites/team/Shared Documents"). Pass decoded path text (spaces, not %20). Must be finalized and confirmed BEFORE invoking this tool. If resolution was ambiguous or the target does not exist, ask the user for confirmation before invoking.

fields.description: Optional rich field definitions. Preferred parameter for explicit field types, choices, required flags, and multiline text behavior. Use this when the user asked for metadata fields but the doclib is otherwise empty and you need to add concrete fields from intent. Include internalName and description for each field.

Must be confirmed BEFORE invocation: if the folder exists, use it; if it is missing, ask the user to confirm creation; if omitted, explicitly ask the user to confirm a suggested destination (or provide one) before invoking. Do not invoke with pending folder disambiguation.

formDescription.description: Optional form description derived from user intent. Derive this from the user request and provide it. If omitted, a generic description is used.

formTitle.description: Optional form title derived from user intent (e.g. "Vendor NDA Intake"). Derive this from the user request and provide it. If omitted, a generic title is used.

maxUploadSizeMb.description: Optional maximum upload size in MB. Use null to keep platform default limit.

requestedFieldDescriptions.description: Optional descriptions aligned by index with requestedFieldNames. If provided, each entry is used as the corresponding field description in the created form.

requestedFieldNames.description: Optional list of user-requested metadata column names to include in the form (e.g. ["Project", "Department", "Due Date"]). If the user wants metadata fields, populate this even when the resolved doclib has no existing metadata columns. Include requested names when provided, reuse existing fields where possible, and do not leave both requestedFieldNames and fields empty when the user is asking for additional metadata.

documentType.description: The output format generated for each submission. "Word" produces .docx documents; "PDF" produces PDFs. Defaults to "Word" when null. Set "PDF" ONLY if the user explicitly asked for PDF output.

fileWebUrl.description: The URL of an existing Word (.docx) document to base the form on. Accepts the URL returned for a selected/in-context file or explicitly selected document search result (including redirect/preview URLs), a direct file URL, or a "Copy link" URL. The source may be in any SharePoint or OneDrive web/geo in the current tenant; external-tenant URLs are not supported. Before any template/form write, search for relevant existing Word documents outside the template library; do NOT use template_finder because template-library items cannot be source documents. Do reads/recon first when the correct source is unknown. If no eligible source is selected or supplied, present relevant document search results and ask the user to choose. If none is suitable, ask whether to create a new draft template and do so only after explicit approval; invoke this tool only after that .docx exists and the user selects or confirms it. For legal documents, prefer approved organizational documents found outside the template library over generated content. Never create, generate, copy, upload, save, guess, or pass an empty source merely to obtain this value.

folderName.description: The name of the new submission folder to create. Required only when shouldCreateNewFolder is true; ignored otherwise. If shouldCreateNewFolder is true and this is null or empty, the tool returns an error asking the caller to provide a folder name.

formName.description: The display name for the form. If null, the tool falls back to a generic default; prefer passing a meaningful name inferred from the document or the contract type (e.g. "NDA Generation Form").

shouldCreateNewFolder.description: Whether to create a new submission folder (named folderName) instead of reusing the currently opened folder. Defaults to false — set false when the user is already inside the folder that should collect submissions (folderServerRelativeUrl); set true (and provide folderName) when a brand-new folder should be created.

existingListFieldDisplayNames.description: **STRONGLY RECOMMENDED whenever existingListFields is non-empty.** Array of SharePoint field display names (user-facing labels, e.g. "Review Count" for internalName "ReviewCount") aligned 1:1 with existingListFields (same length, same order). This value is what the form renders as the field label and is also used to catch duplicate-column attempts when a renamed existing column matches a new element's name. **HOW TO POPULATE:** Read each field's \`Title\` (or equivalent display-name property) from the same \`get_list_schema\` response used for existingListFieldIds, in the same order as the names in existingListFields. **RENAMED COLUMNS — IMPORTANT:** SharePoint list columns can be renamed in list settings without changing their internal name. For example, the built-in "Title" column (internalName="Title") is often renamed to something like "Question", "Task Title", or "Order Number" — the internal name stays "Title" but get_list_schema's \`Title\` property returns the renamed value. Always use that renamed value here, NOT the internal name. Failing to do this causes the form to render the wrong column label (e.g. it will show "Title" instead of "Question") AND may cause the tool to re-create a column that already exists. Only fall back to repeating the internalName when the display name is genuinely unavailable from get_list_schema. Pass an empty array when existingListFields is also empty. Pass \`null\` only when display-name information is unavailable for the entire list — the tool will fall back to using internal names as labels.

existingListFieldIds.description: **REQUIRED whenever existingListFields is non-empty.** Array of SharePoint field GUIDs aligned 1:1 with existingListFields (same length, same order). **HOW TO POPULATE:** Before invoking create_form, you MUST call \`get_list_schema\` against the target list and read each field's \`Id\` (or equivalent GUID property) from the returned schema. Pass those GUIDs here in the same order as the names in existingListFields — do NOT guess, fabricate, or reuse GUIDs from other lists. The tool will NOT generate a substitute GUID for an existing field and will fail if any existing field ID is missing. Pass an empty array only when existingListFields is also empty.

existingListFields.description: **CRITICAL:** Array of INTERNAL names of fields that already exist on the list (one entry per field — this array is aligned 1:1 with existingListFieldIds and existingListFieldDisplayNames, so duplicating entries or mixing internal names with display names breaks the alignment). NEVER include any field in newElements if its internalName OR displayName matches (case-insensitive, ignoring spaces / underscores) OR is semantically similar to ANY field whose internalName appears here OR whose displayName appears in the parallel existingListFieldDisplayNames array. Even if the user explicitly requests to create a column that exists here, DO NOT create it - duplicates are forbidden. Only include truly NEW fields that have no exact or semantically similar match.

formId.description: Optional ID of an existing form to update. Provide the GUID of the form view (the formId returned when the form was created, or visible in the form's edit URL as ...&formId=<id>) ONLY when the user wants to update/edit an existing form. When supplied, the tool updates that form in place instead of creating a new one. Omit this (or leave it empty) to create a brand new form.

formName.description: Optional name/title of an existing form to update when the user refers to the form by name rather than by id, and the formId is unknown. Provide this ONLY when updating an existing form. The tool looks up forms on the list whose title matches this name: if exactly one matches, it is updated in place; if several similarly-named forms match, the tool returns those candidates (with createdBy, description, and field summary) so you can ask the user which one to update, then re-invoke with that form's formId. Prefer formId when you already know it. Omit both formId and formName to create a brand new form.

title.description: The form title shown to users relevant to the form topic or purpose

listBaseType.description: SharePoint list base type identifier. Optional — defaults to "100" (generic list) when omitted. Only set this when the target list is known to use a different base type.

ensureSingleResponsePerUser.description: Set to true to limit each signed-in user to a single response. Use when the user says "one response per person" or similar.

formDisabled.description: Set to true to close the form and stop accepting new responses. Use when the user says things like "close the form" or "stop accepting responses".

formDisabledMessage.description: Custom message shown to respondents when the form is closed/disabled. Only meaningful when formDisabled is true.

formScheduleResponseInfo.description: Start and end dates that bound when the form accepts responses. Required when formScheduleResponses is true.

scheduleResponsesEndDate.description: ISO 8601 date string when response collection should end.

scheduleResponsesStartDate.description: ISO 8601 date string when response collection should start.

formScheduleResponses.description: Set to true to only accept responses during a scheduled window defined by formScheduleResponseInfo.

theme.description: Optional form visual styling. Infer the form type and list type before choosing a theme: requests/approvals should feel calm and professional, feedback/surveys warm and approachable, events/campaigns more energetic, tracking or directory lists clean and neutral, operations/engineering structured, HR/people soft, and facilities/location grounded. Create a premium, polished background that fits that context while prioritizing readability and contrast first. Layer CSS backgrounds from top to bottom: translucent accent/texture layers first, opaque base gradient last. Never put a near-opaque solid or linear gradient first because it hides lower layers. Favor 2-3 large low-opacity radial gradients at different corners/edges for atmospheric depth rather than obvious blobs. Keep palettes restrained, transitions smooth and patterns minimal so white or light text stays highly legible. For custom premium backgrounds, compose 3-5 layers ordered top-to-bottom: transparent/low-opacity accents or textures first, and the opaque base gradient last. Never start with a near-opaque wash such as rgba(..., 0.98), which covers every later layer. Prefer deep navy with blue, violet, teal, or cyan accents; preserve negative space, avoid high-frequency patterns, and use any grid/line/noise-like texture only as a very subtle transparent overlay. Do not use a site URL here, this must point to the list or document library root. The example should not be used as the value for the tool.

siteKey.description: Opaque key identifying the target SharePoint site, obtained from get_site_key. Pass it through unchanged.

user.description: Email address of the user whose access to the file should be removed. This tool does not send a sharing invitation.

camlQuery.description: CAML query to filter items to update. Should contain a <Where> clause. Example: "<Where><Eq><FieldRef Name='Status'/><Value Type='Text'>Active</Value></Eq></Where>"

fieldInternalNames.description: An array of internal names of the fields to update (e.g., ["Status", "Priority"]). These should match the field internal names in the list.

items.description: The exact internalFieldName of the target field (e.g., "Title", "Status", "AssignedTo", "priority"). This value MUST come from fresh get_list_schema output for the target list or from the result of the immediately preceding schema mutation. Never infer it from a display name, user wording, or stale schema output. The internal name may differ from the display name (e.g., "Assigned To" has internalFieldName "AssignedTo").

listId.description: GUID of the SharePoint list/library (e.g., \`3F2504E0-4F89-11D3-9A0C-0305E82C3301\`) — do NOT pass the example value.

listUrl.description: The server-relative URL of the SharePoint list or document library. This URL should start with a forward slash ("/") and include the path to the list, but should not contain the domain name or ".aspx". For an example of the format: "/sites/siteName/Lists/ListName". The example should not be used as the value for the tool.

newValues.description: An array of new values corresponding to each field in fieldInternalNames. The order must match the fieldInternalNames array.

items.description: The value to set for the specified field. This value will replace the current value in the field (if updating) or be set as the initial value (if creating).

siteKey.description: Opaque key identifying the target SharePoint site, obtained from get_site_key. Pass it through unchanged.

items.description: An array of items to update (max 100 per call). Each element specifies the item ID, field names, and new values for one list item. Use this to update multiple items in a single tool call.

fieldInternalNames.description: An array of internal names of the fields to update for this item (e.g., ["Title", "Status", "AssignedTo"]).

This value MUST come from fresh get_list_schema output for the target list or from the result of the immediately preceding schema mutation. itemId.description: The ID of the list item to update. This is a positive integer that uniquely identifies the item within the list.

jobs.description: Array of favorite jobs. Each job adds or removes one item from OneDrive favorites. Use multiple jobs to favorite or unfavorite multiple items, even across different document libraries.

isUnfavorite.description: Set to true to remove the item from favorites, false to add it to favorites.

listFullUrl.description: The full URL of the document library or list. For example, "https://subdomain.sharepoint.com/sites/subdomain/Lists/ListName", "https://contoso-my.sharepoint.com/personal/user_contoso_com/Documents" or "https://onedrive.cloud.microsoft/a@qwerty/Documents". Do not use a site URL here, this must point to the list or document library root. The example should not be used as the value for the tool.

relativePath.description: Path of the item relative to the document library root. Each entry is resolved against listFullUrl. For example, "Reports/Q1/report.pdf" references Documents/Reports/Q1/report.pdf. Do NOT include the document library name (e.g. "Documents") because that is already specified by listFullUrl.
